Cliff Roffey came through for second, Short 3rd., Walker 5th and then the pack Bagnall, Gebbett, Burr, Brickwood and Trower 7th to 11th to make sure of the team race.
Bagnall and Walker ran well for 2nd and 3rd place, followed by the usual crowd with Masters having an easy run whipping up the end of our pack.
John Burr 5th, gave us a good start. 6th was Johnny Butley, first man home for Surrey A.C. and then four more Bels., Masters, Tooby Trower and Bagnall.

After the first half mile we had Masters, Walker and Bagnall in the first 20, with Patterson Baulch, Short, Trower and Bedford in the twenties, and although positions changed a bit, our scoring six were always placed well in the first thirty.

Bagnall was soon prominent, being third after half a mile, with Masters only a few places behind him. Foord of Brighton and Barrett, SAC. were first and second almost from the start and never looked as though they would be replaced.
Roffey and Bagnall gave of their best whilst Dave Baulch ran above form and forced himself past Ingles in the home straight to make sure we had six men home before T.V.H. had three.

At about 2½ miles Cliff was still leading our team and lying about 60th, Pete Bagnall was next, 83rd with Eddie Patterson 85th, next J. Masters 96th, Dave Baulch 118th, Charlie Walker 120th, Eric Gebbett about 150th, and Jack Brown about 160th.
Burr gained a place but Bagnall was passed by Ken Norris, T.V.H. who did 17.42, the fastest time of the day. Walker gained two places and Roffey put us in the lead.

The Blackheath man caught him over the last half mile and Peter Bagnall went off 5 yards down. Meanwhile Collis had run very well to pull up the "B" Team from 17th to 10th position and Carter had maintained the Vets' position.

The first track event was the newly instituted 6 miles and at the crack of the gun, 12 runners were off to a fast start with Eric Gebbett showing the way at the end of the first mile in 4.59. followed by Bagnall, Smart, Baulch and Hitchcock.
Short, Bagnall and Patterson, please oblige. It will be noted that the post-war boom in athletics shows itself in performances by club members.
Half way round the first lap, Bagnall, Paterson, Short, Masters and Baulch were all between 20th and 30th in that order and Gebbett and Trower were in the next dozen.
He was accompanied over the first five miles by Pat Newell, followed by Walker, Bagnall, Short and Gebbett, but at this stage Short retired.

Charlie Walker took the lead quickly, with Baulch, Bagnall and Flanagan on his heels. Round the first lap of the Common, Flanagan went to the front but was not allowed to keep his nose ahead for long.
Pete Bagnall set out from Old Palace Yard, Westminster, on the first stroke of ten by Big Ben. Just before Chelsea Bridge, Ian Boyd running for Herne Hill, jumped the field and began to draw away.
The boys however, ran like heroes especially in the latter part of the race and more than compensated for an off-day by Pete Bagnall on the first leg.
Ex-members, Geoff Goode and Steve Charlton were seen running for their new clubs. Semi-retired Bagnall would have been our third scoring man with his 56th place!!
